gloss_short: asks if someone is telling the truth; "for real?"
origin: Not in the CLM dictionary or any Wiktionary MTE/MLE category; the only lexicographic support is the Wikipedia Multicultural Toronto English interjections section. Corpus support is reddit/YouTube only. The surface parallel to "say word" invites an AAVE-origin guess, but no source actually attests that derivation for this specific phrase, so origin/region status is left unclear rather than asserted.

gloss_short: instant enthusiastic agreement; "say no more, I'm in"
origin: Alteration of "say no more"; now a widely generalized Gen-Z/internet phrase, heavily attested in Toronto reddit and boxcutter corpora.

gloss_short: enough said; also a casual goodbye
origin: General English idiom broadened with a Commonwealth/MLE-MTE farewell sense; Wiktionary explicitly tags the farewell sense's categories with both Multicultural London English and Multicultural Toronto English.

gloss_short: expresses disbelief; "really? no way!"
origin: African American Vernacular English (per CLM dictionary entry), heavily naturalized into Toronto speech.

gloss_short: nickname for Scarborough, Toronto
origin: Clipped form of the Toronto neighbourhood name Scarborough; listed in the Wiktionary MTE category.

gloss_short: to pick someone up / give them a ride
origin: Tagged Multicultural Toronto English in Wiktionary; also listed in a Narcity Toronto slang glossary.

gloss_short: a request for someone to come pick you up
origin: Narcity Toronto slang glossary entry; imperative form of the MTE verb "scoop".

gloss_short: to fight; a physical fight or brawl
origin: General English/AAVE slang for fighting; not in Toronto Wiktionary categories but heavily recurrent in Toronto street/meme media (Goon Scrap DVDs).

gloss_short: means "got it, understood"; also a confirming tag
origin: Jamaican Patois interjection, naturalized heavily into Toronto/MTE speech via the Jamaican-Canadian community.

gloss_short: girl, girlfriend, or attractive young woman
origin: African American Vernacular English

gloss_short: secret secondary romantic/sexual partner
origin: Multicultural London English 'ting' (person/thing placeholder) + 'side'

gloss_short: onomatopoeia for tires screeching / speeding off
origin: Onomatopoeic, popularized by Southern US rap (Waka Flocka Flame, Chief Keef)

gloss_short: close ally/crew member, or an untrustworthy person
origin: African American Vernacular English/gang slang ('slime' = crew/loyalty term), with a locally noted negative shift toward 'untrustworthy person' in Toronto usage

gloss_short: an untrustworthy, backstabbing person
origin: General English figurative sense (treacherous person), reinforced by MTE/MLE slang usage

gloss_short: desperate, cringe, or trying way too hard
origin: Likely Jamaican Patois 'beg' (to want/desire, or a 'beg friend' = hanger-on); not confirmed Toronto-specific coinage.

gloss_short: fine, no big deal (patois); also weak, not tough
origin: Jamaican Patois (per Wikipedia Toronto-slang page); the 'weak' sense is shared broadly with AAVE/hip-hop slang.

gloss_short: come outside; let's go (Somali)
origin: Somali

gloss_short: to rob/steal from someone; a robbery
origin: AAVE/drill slang, widely used across North American and UK drill scenes, prominent in Toronto drill lyrics (Casper TNG, Pressa).

gloss_short: style (combination of 'style' and 'ease')
origin: North American skate/snowboard slang blend of 'style' + 'ease'.

gloss_short: exclamation for a great bargain; also 'appropriated' (of culture/slang)
origin: Past participle of 'steal', generalized into slang exclamation and appropriation-commentary usage.

gloss_short: sentence-final tag: 'though', 'to be honest', pronounced 'still'
origin: English discourse-marker 'still', respelled 'styll'; documented as shared between Toronto (MTE) and London (MLE) slang via Wiktionary category tags.

gloss_short: to suck air through the teeth to show annoyance/disapproval
origin: Caribbean/West African gesture, documented in the CLM Toronto slang dictionary

gloss_short: suspicious, shady, or untrustworthy
origin: Clipping of 'suspicious'/'suspect'; general English informal usage, popularized globally via Among Us

gloss_short: an attractive, smooth-talking man with the ladies
origin: Toronto/GTA slang, popularized by Ramriddlz and Drake's song 'Sweeterman'

gloss_short: contraction of 'what's wrong'
origin: Contraction of 'what's wrong'; attested in UK slang sources and Toronto reddit use

gloss_short: 'got it' / 'understood', an agreement backchannel
origin: Likely derived from Jamaican Patois 'seen' (backchannel of agreement/understanding)

gloss_short: nickname for Toronto
origin: Coined by Toronto rapper K4CE (K-Force) in the early 1990s as a Toronto nickname

gloss_short: to steal
origin: Jamaican Patois 'teef' (from 'thief'), also present in Nigerian English and shared with Multicultural London English

gloss_short: a hotel or hotel room
origin: Clipped from '(ho)tel/(mo)tel' + -y; tagged Canada/Multicultural Toronto English in Wiktionary

gloss_short: said when a slap-worthy dumb comment is made
origin: Documented in a Toronto slang video series ('The Green Line'); older general use also attested on Urban Dictionary outside Toronto

gloss_short: that's hilarious/funny
origin: Use of 'jokes' as an adjective meaning funny is documented in both Toronto and London multicultural youth slang

gloss_short: that's lame or disappointing
origin: General hip-hop/AAVE-derived slang use of 'weak' for 'lame', also listed in a Toronto slang roundup

gloss_short: that's crazy or unbelievable
origin: Widespread general North American/Gen-Z slang; also listed in a Toronto slang roundup

gloss_short: Toronto, named for its 416 area code
origin: Toronto telephone area code (416)

gloss_short: Nickname for the city of Toronto
origin: Shortened from 'T-Dot', itself derived from the initialism 'T.O.' for Toronto

gloss_short: Tim Hortons, the Canadian coffee-and-donuts chain
origin: Diminutive of 'Tim Hortons', named for Canadian hockey player Tim Horton

gloss_short: Generalized word for 'thing'; also an attractive person/casual partner
origin: Jamaican Patois 'ting' (th-stopped form of English 'thing')

gloss_short: a gun (street slang); also a foolish/used person
origin: General English insult sense; firearm sense shared Multicultural Toronto English / Multicultural London English street slang

gloss_short: a gun (firearm), street slang
origin: tool + diminutive suffix -ie; firearm sense shared between Multicultural Toronto English and Multicultural London English

gloss_short: I swear / for real, on my heart
origin: Toronto-specific coinage of unknown ultimate etymology; popularized via Random Order Studios sketches and Toronto drill lyrics (Pressa, Snowd4y)

gloss_short: to arrive at, go to, or get out to a place
origin: Jamaican Patois

gloss_short: yeah, I agree — said to affirm or acknowledge a statement
origin: Standard English adjective 'true', repurposed as a discourse marker; documented in multiple Toronto slang glossaries

gloss_short: to smoke, especially weed
origin: Canadian slang, listed on the Multicultural Toronto English Wikipedia page under Verbs

gloss_short: to get hyped up, especially at a party
origin: Jamaican Patois 'tun' (turn), used across the Caribbean diaspora and in Toronto nightlife slang

gloss_short: suddenly, quickly, in no time
origin: Jamaican/Caribbean English, in both the Wiktionary Multicultural Toronto English and Multicultural London English categories

gloss_short: a case of 24 beers
origin: General Canadian English (Beer Store terminology), not Toronto-specific

gloss_short: uncle; respectful term for an older man
origin: Somali, per the Multicultural Toronto English Wikipedia page

gloss_short: angry, annoyed, or irritated
origin: Jamaican Patois 'vex'

gloss_short: greeting: what's up / what's going on
origin: Jamaican Patois 'wah gwan'

gloss_short: I swear to God; emphatic oath
origin: Arabic 'wallahi' (by God), via Somali

gloss_short: hey!/oi! — Somali term to get a man's attention
origin: Somali

gloss_short: describes someone/something as worthless, bad, or contemptible
origin: Jamaican Patois

gloss_short: a worthless, no-good, immature person (usually male)
origin: Jamaican Patois

gloss_short: a worthless, silly, or immature young person; insult
origin: Jamaican Patois

gloss_short: slang: to shoot, stab, or seriously hurt/kill someone
origin: Multicultural London/Toronto English

gloss_short: greeting: 'what are you doing?' / 'what's going on?'
origin: Jamaican Patois

gloss_short: Flirting with someone, pre-dating stage
origin: General Canadian/North American youth slang, prominently documented in Toronto slang glossaries paired with the tag 'styll'.

gloss_short: A car, especially a nice one
origin: African-American Vernacular English / hip-hop slang for 'car', broadly adopted including in Toronto rap and street speech.

gloss_short: Girlfriend or wife-like partner
origin: African-American English endearment ('wife' + -y), listed on the Toronto slang Wikipedia noun list.

gloss_short: Crazy or unusual (describing someone's actions)
origin: Jamaican Patois

gloss_short: Oral sex (crude slang)
origin: Toronto slang coinage; Wiktionary quotations are sourced to r/Torontology and Twitter, and genius annotations explicitly label it 'a slang term used in Toronto for oral sex'.

gloss_short: Initialism greeting, 'what you saying?'
origin: Initialism of 'what you saying', from Multicultural London English texting slang, also tagged MTE.

gloss_short: Come on, let's go, hurry up
origin: Arabic ياالله (yā allāh, 'oh God' / 'c'mon'), used generally across Arabic-speaking diaspora communities including in Toronto.

gloss_short: Flirty pickup-line phrase used by Toronto mans
origin: Toronto slang, documented in a local glossary as a flirting pickup line.

gloss_short: an approving exclamation, like admiring "oooh, nice"
origin: Toronto glossary (Narcity); no clear ethnolinguistic source given

gloss_short: to be finished/done for, referencing crime-scene tape
origin: Toronto MTE coinage referencing crime-scene tape imagery

gloss_short: casual greeting/address, like "hey man"
origin: Toronto slang glossary (Narcity)

gloss_short: you all, you guys (plural you)
origin: MTE/MLE pronoun system ("mans" as a plural/generic pronoun)

origin: Jamaican Patois

origin: Jamaican Patois ("youth")

origin: Jamaican Patois
